query: Consider the following context: The recent trend of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) was studied extensively for their promising mechanical properties, but individual constituents' effects have remained unexplored. In that context, which method can be used for the effects of changing the percentage of elements of HfNbTaTiZr-HEA on the mechanical properties, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The mechanical properties of HfNbTaTiZr-HEA, such as yield strength and ductility, will be significantly influenced by the variation of elemental percentages, particularly the ratio of Hf to other elements, due to differences in atomic size and electronic structure.
generation.intervention: Systematic variation of elemental percentages using a design of experiments (DoE) approach
generation.conditions: Room temperature, varying strain rates and loading conditions
generation.structural_mediator: Atomic size and electronic structure differences among constituent elements
generation.mechanism: Changes in elemental percentages alter the lattice distortion, electronic bonding, and dislocation dynamics, leading to variations in mechanical properties
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in Hf content will lead to an increase in yield strength, while an increase in Ti content will lead to an increase in ductility
generation.baseline: The mechanical properties of the base HfNbTaTiZr-HEA composition
generation.boundary: The limits of solubility and phase stability in the HfNbTaTiZr-HEA system
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of the effects of individual elements on mechanical properties, and the potential interactions between elements

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing and compression testing of HfNbTaTiZr-HEA samples with systematically varied elemental percentages, combined with DFT or MD simulations to understand the underlying mechanisms
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the measured mechanical properties do not correlate with the predicted trends based on elemental percentages, the hypothesis is falsified
